verdicts.reason: Y (strongest point: ambition rating guards against cut-ambition revisions, panel family excluded from the verifier, explicit kill thresholds) beats X (strongest point: clean two-order gate with no-reasons control) because it closes X's named failure modes and makes the test decisive.

Y fits tau from saved rating residuals, guards against variance-seeking on under-compared items and gates on label kappa with explicit kill criteria, whereas X hard-codes tau at 0.5 SD with no falsifier.

Y's witness-value flip directly blocks rigged always-FAIL checks and its size-normalised score with 10-brief kill criteria and an ambition guard makes the test decisive, while X tests on one brief with no kill rule.

Y re-extracts claims from revised text and penalises struck load-bearing claims, closing the overfit-to-frozen-check and claim-weakening gaps, and its matched-token prose-feedback control isolates the loop's value.
Both share the same MATURE mechanism, but Y re-ranks finals on fresh comparisons to avoid winner's-curse selection and adds a kill threshold on the held-out child-beats-parent rate.
Y's two-panel fit-on-A/score-on-B design directly addresses the Goodhart failure X names, and it adds a bootstrap kill criterion on AUC gain.
Y adds a 40% cap on judge sampling to avoid concentrating votes on a noisy a_j and a 2x2 test separating reweighting from allocation with a bootstrap kill rule.
Y shrinks operator priors toward the global win rate and pairs the primary test by brief with a kill interval, correcting X's per-contest power calculation that ignores within-brief correlation.

Y's placebo paraphrase through the same gate measures style bias empirically, uses two other-family judges, and replays offline on saved runs with kill conditions, whereas X's single verifier is a shared-style risk it only lists.

Y makes the method non-inferior by construction (identical to top-3 for diverse finalists, capped mean-of-3 loss) and fits tau from data, so it is a costless null at worst and directly targets the benchmark's win rate against the single agent.
Y adds codebase-probe checks so feasibility claims in this qualitative brief become checkable, measures the checkable fraction first, and gives sparse cards the median score rather than last place.

Y works standalone with a fallback extractor, caps token cost at 1.4x, reverts cards left with too few claims and is testable offline on saved finalists, whereas X depends on a ledger existing and costs about 2x.
Y's gate judges come from a family that is neither the ranker's nor the panel's, so it breaks the in-loop overfit that X only mitigates, and it measures the overfit gap with a kill threshold.

Y's staged design (sign-constrained nuisance-only weights first, needing about 5 briefs, with a within-run conditional logit) is feasible with realistic label counts and has an oracle-headroom kill test, while X needs about 15 labelled briefs before doing anything.

Y adds a shared verbosity-bias term and label-free probe calibration of position and self-preference biases so most of the model fits without external labels, with shrinkage bounding noise and a tau kill threshold.

Y warm-starts on about 800 saved contests with no new runs and runs an offline chi-square kill test before the expensive 30-brief stage, and it uses a non-mutator judge family to reduce memorising judge quirks.
